author: NorthEast News Desk
body: At least 21 people were killed in a crash involving two minibus taxis and an SUV in South Africa’s Western Cape, according to authorities cited by The Associated Press. The collision happened Sunday night on a road between Prince Albert and Leeu-Gamka.
The two taxis collided head-on before the SUV became involved, the AP reported. Three people were declared dead after being taken to a hospital, and four others were reported in serious condition.

The crash closed the N1 highway while emergency crews worked at the scene. Officials warned that the death toll could change as investigators identify victims and assess the condition of those hospitalized.

An investigation has been opened into what caused the collision. The road connects communities in a remote part of the province, and the number of passengers and the sequence of impacts were still being reviewed in the initial reports.
The report remains subject to further verified updates as officials continue reviewing the circumstances.
dek: At least 21 people died in a head-on collision in South Africa’s Western Cape, authorities said, with the death toll potentially changing as the investigation continues.
headline: At least 21 killed in South Africa crash involving two taxis and SUV
